people.name: Eleazar
people.description: Aged priest and lawyer who was flogged and burned rather than eat swine's flesh.
people.descent_note: Called 'the descendant of Aaron' (7:12): priestly descent, not a parent.
people.identity_note: Same martyr as Eleazar of 2MA 6:18-31 (2MA calls him a scribe aged 90); same new_id used in 2MA. No age is stated in 4MA. Distinct from Eleazar the priest of 3MA.

people.name: Mother of the seven brothers
people.description: Aged mother who urged her seven sons to die for the law and threw herself on the pyre.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom. 17:1 reports she threw herself on the pile; 2MA 7:41 simply says she died.

people.name: Father of the seven brothers
people.description: Husband of the mother, who taught the sons the law and the prophets and died before the persecution.
people.identity_note: Mentioned only in 4MA (the mother's speech, 18:7-19; also 10:2).

people.name: First of the seven brothers
people.description: Oldest brother, broken on the wheel and burned.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Second of the seven brothers
people.description: Second brother, flayed with iron gauntlets.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Third of the seven brothers
people.description: Third brother, dismembered and broken on the wheel.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Fourth of the seven brothers
people.description: Fourth brother, whose tongue was cut out.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Fifth of the seven brothers
people.description: Fifth brother, who volunteered and was bent on the wheel.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Sixth of the seven brothers
people.description: Sixth brother, 'quite a youth', roasted and pierced with spits.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Seventh (youngest) of the seven brothers
people.description: Seventh and youngest brother, who threw himself into the pans.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Joseph
people.description: Patriarch praised for self-control; his imprisonment was taught to the brothers.

people.name: Moses
people.description: Lawgiver who restrained his anger against Dathan and Abiram.

people.name: Dathan
people.description: Rebel against Moses.

people.name: Abiram
people.description: Rebel against Moses.

people.name: Jacob
people.description: Patriarch who cursed the anger of Simeon and Levi.

people.name: Simeon
people.description: Son of Jacob who slew the Shechemites.

people.name: Levi
people.description: Son of Jacob who slew the Shechemites.

people.name: David
people.description: King who poured out the water his soldiers fetched from the enemy camp.

people.name: Seleucus
people.description: King of Asia who funded the temple service; father of Antiochus Epiphanes according to 4MA.
people.identity_note: 3:20 'Seleucus Nicanor' (i.e. Nicator, the dynasty's founder's epithet) is applied by the author to the king of Onias' time, Seleucus IV; mapped to seleucus-iv-philopator (same id as 2MA).

people.name: Simon
people.description: Opponent of Onias who informed Apollonius of the temple treasure.
people.identity_note: Same person as Simon the temple guardian of 2MA 3-4; same new_id.

people.name: Onias
people.description: High priest for life, who prayed for Apollonius and was deposed by Antiochus.
people.identity_note: Same as Onias of 2MA 3-4; same new_id.

people.name: Apollonius
people.description: Military governor of Syria, Phoenicia and Cilicia who tried to seize the temple treasure and was struck down by angels.
people.identity_note: 4MA's retelling of 2MA 3 gives Apollonius the role played by Heliodorus in 2MA; mapped to the governor of 2MA 3:5 (apollonius-of-tarsus).

people.name: Antiochus Epiphanes
people.description: Seleucid tyrant who tortured Eleazar and the seven brothers.
people.identity_note: 4MA 4:15 calls him the son of Seleucus (IV); historically he was Seleucus IV's brother. Recorded as stated. Same new_id as 2MA.

people.name: Jason
people.description: Brother of Onias made high priest, who hellenized the nation.
people.identity_note: Same as 2MA's Jason; same new_id.

people.name: Ptolemy
people.description: Egyptian king with whom Antiochus IV was at war.
people.identity_note: Unnamed epithet here; mapped to Ptolemy VI Philometor (same id as 2MA) by historical context.

people.name: Abraham
people.description: Patriarch held up as the model of fortitude.

people.name: Aaron
people.description: Priest who stopped the plague with a censer; ancestor of Eleazar.

people.name: Isaac
people.description: Patriarch offered up by Abraham.

people.name: Noah
people.description: Builder of the ark, used as a simile for the mother.

people.name: Daniel
people.description: Delivered from the lions' den.

people.name: Misael
people.description: One of the three young men in the furnace.
people.identity_note: 13:9 'the three young men in Assyria' refers to the trio unnamed.

people.name: Ananias
people.description: One of the three young men in the furnace.
people.identity_note: Greek form of Hananiah.

people.name: Azarias
people.description: One of the three young men in the furnace.
people.identity_note: Greek form of Azariah.

people.name: Abel
people.description: Slain by Cain.

people.name: Cain
people.description: Slayer of Abel.

people.name: Phinehas
people.description: The zealous priest.

people.name: Esaias
people.description: Prophet Isaiah, quoted on passing through fire.

people.name: Solomon
people.description: Author of proverbs.

people.name: Ezekiel
people.description: Prophet of the dry bones.

excluded_names.Nicanor: epithet in 'Seleucus Nicanor' (3:20), not a separate person

notes: 4 Maccabees is a philosophical discourse retelling 2MA 3-7. Shared ids with 2MA: eleazar-martyr, mother-of-seven-brothers, seven-brothers-son-1..7, antiochus-iv-epiphanes, onias-iii, jason-high-priest, seleucus-iv-philopator, simon-temple-guardian, apollonius-of-tarsus, ptolemy-vi-philometor. The unnamed father of the seven (18:7-19) appears only here. The mother's speech (18:9) says the sons' father died when they reached maturity; 16:9 implies some sons were married. Sons' parent links cite 8:2 (seven brothers with their mother) and 10:2 (the third brother: 'the father of those who are dead is my father also'). No explicit ages stated (Eleazar is 'advanced in years'; the 90 years is from 2MA 6:24). 'The tyrant' throughout = Antiochus IV; refs list a representative set. The two young soldiers who fetched water for David (3:12) are an unnamed pair and are not recorded.
